verification_method.registry: ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, full study records retrieved live 2026-07-30. Per-arm values, unitOfMeasure, denoms and group TITLES read directly from resultsSection.outcomeMeasuresModule.

verification_method.independence: Every number was re-derived in this session. The pilot's figures were used as a hypothesis to test, not as a source. Where they disagree with this file, this file is the verified value - see 'corrections_to_the_pilot'.

corrections_to_the_pilot.evidence: R 4.6.0 metafor rma.mh returns pred 1.9748, ci.lb 1.0411, ci.ub 3.7457. The point estimate in the pilot is correct; its interval is too narrow.
corrections_to_the_pilot.why_it_matters: The pilot's interval overstates precision. The verified interval only just excludes 1 (p = 0.037) and the HKSJ-adjusted interval crosses it. The DIRECTION of the correction is unaffected; its certainty is.

per_trial.why_the_previous_values_were_wrong: Both ledger counts were 18 because 18 is recoverable BOTH as 3.0% of 599 (placebo) and as 5.7% of 315 (apixaban 2.5 mg BID). The denominators carried (611, 317) are the PUBLICATION's randomised n, while the counts are only recoverable from the REGISTRY's analysed denominators (599, 315) - counts and denominators came from different documents, and the arms were transposed.
per_trial.corroboration: PMID 19470889 abstract, verbatim: 'Compared with placebo, apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily (hazard ratio, 1.78; 95% confidence interval, 0.91 to 3.48; P=0.09) and 10 mg once daily (hazard ratio, 2.45; 95% confidence interval, 1.31 to 4.61; P=0.005) resulted in a dose-dependent increase in major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding.' The published HR 1.78 and the corrected crude OR 1.956 point the same way. The pre-correction ledger pointed the opposite way.
per_trial.disclosed_limitation: Only the 2.5 mg BID arm is pooled. Three higher-dose apixaban arms (10 mg QD n=318, 10 mg BID n=248, 20 mg QD n=221; 787 patients) are not pooled; the two highest-dose arms were discontinued by the Data Monitoring Committee for excess total bleeding. Stated on the badge.

why_the_previous_values_were_wrong.root_cause: A RATE read as a PROPORTION.
why_the_previous_values_were_wrong.proof: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00831441 posts the primary with unitOfMeasure 'percentage of participants/100-pt years' - an incidence rate over person-time. Verified live: group OG000 'Placebo' value 13.96 denom 3687; group OG001 'Apixaban 5 mg BID' value 13.20 denom 3705. 3687 x 13.96/100 = 514.65 -> the ledger's 515. 3705 x 13.20/100 = 489.06 -> the ledger's 489. Both reproduce to under one unit. Neither count appears in any document.
why_the_previous_values_were_wrong.second_defect: Arms swapped. tN = 3687 is the PLACEBO denominator; cN = 3705 is apixaban's. The registry lists Placebo as OG000 and the extraction bound arms by index.
why_the_previous_values_were_wrong.third_defect: The row carried the genuine published HR 0.95 (favouring apixaban) beside counts giving a crude RR of 1.058 (favouring placebo). The app's own window.__verdict had already recorded '2 AACT outcome-direction divergence(s)' and the badge rendered green over it.

per_trial.note: APPRAISE-2 was terminated early for excess major bleeding with apixaban without a counterbalancing reduction in ischaemic events. That termination is a finding about APPRAISE-2, which is NOT in this pool - external corroboration of the pooled result's direction, not the pooled result itself.

per_trial.quarantine_reason: Wrong PICO. AUGUSTUS randomised patients with ATRIAL FIBRILLATION who had an ACS or PCI and compared apixaban against a VITAMIN K ANTAGONIST - not against placebo on top of antiplatelet therapy. It is also the only open-label (masking NONE) and only phase 4 trial in an otherwise double-blind phase 2-3 set, and a 2x2 factorial that no single 2x2 table can represent without stating which factor is estimated and that the other is marginalised over.

citation_correction.was_actually: Lopes RD et al. 'An open-label, 2x2 factorial, randomized controlled trial to evaluate the safety of apixaban vs. vitamin K antagonist and aspirin vs. placebo ... Rationale and design of the AUGUSTUS trial.' Am Heart J 2018;200:17-23. DOI 10.1016/j.ahj.2018.03.001. citation_correction.now: PMID 30883055 - Lopes RD et al. 'Antithrombotic Therapy after Acute Coronary Syndrome or PCI in Atrial Fibrillation.' N Engl J Med 2019;380(16):1509-1524. DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1817083.

why_the_previous_values_were_wrong.root_cause: A level-of-aggregation mismatch, compounded by a rate read as a proportion.
why_the_previous_values_were_wrong.arithmetic_origin: 1153 x 24.66/100 = 284.33 -> the ledger 284; 1153 x 35.79/100 = 412.66 -> the ledger 413. Across all four reproductions (both trials) the maximum deviation is 0.3413, so the bound stated on the page is <= 0.3413. A measured reproduction, not a claim about intent.
why_the_previous_values_were_wrong.the_denominator: 1153 is a REAL registry denominator. NCT02415400 randomised 1153 / 1153 / 1154 / 1154 across the four cells of its 2x2 factorial (total 4614), so 1153 is the size of each APIXABAN cell. The defect is that a factorial-CELL denominator was paired with a FACTOR-LEVEL marginal rate: the posted 24.66 and 35.79 ('Percentage per year') belong to the apixaban and VKA factor levels, analysed on 2290 and 2259. Compounding it, the apixaban-side cell denominator was applied to the VKA arm as well, whose cells are 1154.
why_the_previous_values_were_wrong.ci_defect: The ledger's upper CI was 0.82; the publication states 0.81.

per_trial.why_no_counts_are_asserted: The publication reports percentages, not counts, and the registry posts a per-year rate. Back-computing counts from either would repeat the exact error being corrected. No per-arm count is written for this trial. This is the 'if a count cannot be verified, mark it, do not fabricate' rule applied literally.
per_trial.arm_orientation_note: Unlike the three APPRAISE trials, this registry lists Apixaban FIRST (OG000). This row was therefore the one row of four whose arms were NOT transposed - which is itself evidence that the previous extraction bound arms by index rather than by name.

pooled_result.outcome: ISTH major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding
pooled_result.population: Acute coronary syndrome, on standard antiplatelet therapy

before.why_meaningless: Three rows contributed bleeding outcomes and one an ischaemic composite; two rows' counts were manufactured; three rows' arms were transposed.

after.r_validation: R 4.6.0 metafor rma.mh: pred 1.9748, ci.lb 1.0411, ci.ub 3.7457, pval 0.0372
after.interpretation_status: PRELIMINARY / exploratory - see the 'preliminary' block. Supports the reversal and the direction, not a precise magnitude.

pooled_result.app_panel_agreement: The app's own analysis panel independently recomputes and displays OR 1.97 (1.04-3.74), k=2, via inverse-variance random effects with tau^2 = 0 (so DerSimonian-Laird and Paule-Mandel coincide). Verified in a live browser render, not inferred from the file.
pooled_result.sign_change: The correction reverses the conclusion from benefit to harm. This is a PROVENANCE CORRECTION, not a result that got worse - the evidence did not change; the app was wrong. The direction is independently corroborated on the identical endpoint by APPRAISE-2 (rate ratio 2.686, same direction), a trial not in the pool. Direction only: a rate ratio over person-time and an odds ratio over a fixed follow-up are different estimands on different scales, so the two magnitudes are not comparable and none is claimed.

fragility_disclosed.hksj: The HKSJ-adjusted interval is 0.03-124.7 and CROSSES 1. At k=2 HKSJ uses t with df=1 and is uninformative; the app's own panel flags the discordance.
fragility_disclosed.statement: The DIRECTION (harm) is robust and independently corroborated by APPRAISE-2's TIMI major bleeding HR 2.59 (1.50-4.46). The P-VALUE is not robust. Both are stated on the badge.

sensitivity.spec: Both rows on registry-analysed denominators (APPRAISE-J 4/98 vs 1/51)
Both rows on publication randomised denominators (APPRAISE-1 18/317 vs 18/611)

pooled_result.phase2_restriction_justification: The count-based pool is phase-2-only. This follows from the MEASURE available, not from a judgement that phase-3 evidence should be dropped: the phase-3 trial reports this endpoint as a rate, and a count-based estimator cannot consume a rate without person-time or counts. It does not select a favourable subset - on the identical endpoint the excluded phase-3 trial shows harm in the SAME DIRECTION. Direction only: a rate ratio over person-time and an odds ratio over a fixed follow-up are different estimands on different scales, so the two magnitudes are not comparable and none is claimed. Restricting to phase 3 instead would leave no count-based estimate at all.

engine_changes_and_why.why: Correcting the phases to their true values (II, II) triggered the app's own phase-2 exclusion, which would have emptied the analysis pool. The entire coherent evidence base for apixaban vs placebo on this outcome in ACS IS phase 2. The default exclusion is switched off for this app and the phase-2 status of both pooled trials is stated on the badge and in every ledger row.
engine_changes_and_why.honesty_note: This is disclosed, not hidden. The alternative - leaving the phases falsely marked III so the engine would pool them - would have been dishonest by construction.

engine_changes_and_why.why: Under AUTO the app pools a RISK RATIO whenever not every trial carries a published HR. Pinning OR makes the displayed estimate the same quantity as the R-validated Mantel-Haenszel figure on the badge, so the two surfaces cannot be read as contradicting each other.
